summary: Climber fell on the final pitch of a technical climb on Lone Eagle Peak and sustained serious injuries; Flight For Life located the pair and a Buckley Black Hawk helicopter with Rocky Mountain Rescue hoisted the patient before sunset
location: Lone Eagle Peak, Indian Peaks Wilderness
responding_agency: Flight For Life, Buckley AFB Black Hawk, Rocky Mountain Rescue
notes: Date inferred: July 3 article says responders acted 'yesterday'; county not stated (Lone Eagle Peak is in the Indian Peaks Wilderness, Grand County side) CSAR narrative (coloradosar.org): GCSAR paged just before 2:00 PM on multiple SPOT distress activations; subject a 52-year-old experienced climber who fell ~20 ft plus a 10-20 ft roll ten feet above his last protection on a ten-pitch route on the north face near Monarch Lake, with suspected head/back/rib injuries; mission leader Greg Foley + CSAR coordinator Bruce Fosdick (Douglas County SAR) requested a Buckley Black Hawk on standby, dispatched six RMRG members to Boulder Airport, and had FFL Lifeguard 1 fly over (Lifeguard 2 later stood by); a GCSAR ground team hiked in from Monarch Lake; the Black Hawk hoisted the patient on the fourth attempt in 30-mph gusts and landed at Granby Airport ~8:30 PM, transferring him to FFL for a Denver hospital.
